faqs.question: What is the Mya 4 Reaction Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a 4-zone automated reaction station used for process development, Design of Experiment work, scale-up, and reaction screening, with each zone independently controlled.

faqs.question: How independent are the four zones really?
faqs.answer: Genuinely independent, with up to 200°C of temperature difference tolerated between adjacent zones, thanks to high-performance insulation.

faqs.question: How do I set up two reactions at very different temperatures side by side?
faqs.answer: Assign each reaction to a separate zone and set its temperature independently; as long as the difference between adjacent zones stays within 200°C, both run without interfering with each other.

faqs.question: How do I cool a reaction without a separate chiller?
faqs.answer: Use the built-in Peltier cooling, which reaches -25°C directly from a standard tap water supply, with no separate chiller unit required.

faqs.question: What vessels does the Mya 4 support?
faqs.answer: Vials and tubes from 2 to 20 mL, round bottom flasks from 25 to 250 mL, and process reaction vessels from 50 to 400 mL.

faqs.question: Can I mix magnetic and overhead stirring across zones?
faqs.answer: Yes. Magnetic stirring is standard on every zone, and the optional Mya Compact overhead stirrer can be used on adjacent zones alongside it.

faqs.question: What's the difference between the Control Pad and PC Control Software?
faqs.answer: The Control Pad is supplied as standard for manual or automated profile operation; the optional PC Control Software adds integration and control of third-party devices like pumps, balances, and pH sensors.

faqs.question: Does the Mya 4 support 24/7 unattended operation?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is a core design intent, with automated profiles and full data-logging supporting unattended runs.

faqs.question: Can the Mya 4 export reaction data?
faqs.answer: Yes, in CSV format, from either the Control Pad or the PC Control Software.

faqs.answer: The price depends on your vessel, stirring, and control configuration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

longForm.heroLead: Four zones, each up to 200°C apart. Cooled by tap water, not a separate chiller. Running four reactions at once usually means four separate setups, each fighting for bench space and each needing its own cooling. Mya 4 doesn't ask for that. Four fully independent zones sit close together, yet high-performance insulation holds up to a 200°C difference between adjacent zones, so a reflux at 150°C and a cryogenic reaction at -20°C can run side by side without interfering with each other. Cooling comes from Peltier technology and tap water, reaching -25°C with no separate chiller to plumb in. Heating runs from -30°C to +180°C at the block, built for genuine 24/7 unattended operation with full data-logging. Choose magnetic or overhead stirring per zone, mix both across adjacent positions, and run vessels from 2 mL vials up to 400 mL process vessels on the same station.

sections.title: Zone Independence and Temperature Control
body: Running genuinely different reactions side by side depends on the zones not talking to each other thermally, and that's the specific engineering problem Mya 4 solves.

High-performance insulation holds up to a 200°C difference between adjacent zones, so a high-temperature reflux and a low-temperature crystallization can run next to each other without either affecting the other's result. Cooling itself comes from Peltier technology reaching -25°C directly from a tap water supply, removing the need for a separate recirculating chiller entirely. Block and solution temperature are tracked separately, since what the block reads and what's actually happening in the vessel aren't quite the same thing.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Control Pad and the PC Control Software?
faqs.answer: The Control Pad, included as standard, caps experiments at 30 steps of up to 16 hours each with no third-party device control; the PC Software removes that step limit entirely and adds control of up to 16 third-party devices from one screen.

faqs.question: Do I need the PC Control Software?
faqs.answer: Only if your protocols exceed 30 steps or 16 hours per step, or if you need to control external devices like pumps, balances, or sensors alongside the Mya 4.

faqs.question: How do I control a third-party device with the Mya 4?
faqs.answer: Upgrade to the PC Control Software, confirm your device is on the supported list (syringe pumps, pH sensors, peristaltic pumps, and others), and install the relevant device driver.

faqs.question: How do I try the software before buying it?
faqs.answer: Download the free demo version, which simulates device control and lets you build and test schedules without needing the physical Mya 4 connected.

faqs.question: Can I move my PC Software license to a different computer?
faqs.answer: No. Once the license is activated on a PC, it cannot be moved, so confirm your installation PC before activating.

faqs.question: What are the minimum PC requirements for the software?
faqs.answer: Windows 7, 8, 10, or 11, a dual-core 1.9 GHz processor, 2 GB RAM minimum (4 GB recommended), 30 GB hard disk at 5,400 rpm, and Intel HD Graphics.

faqs.question: Does the Control Pad support multi-user operation?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is included as standard, letting different users run experiments independently across the four zones.

faqs.question: Can I export reports from the Control Pad?
faqs.answer: Yes, in CSV format via USB memory stick; the PC Software additionally offers a Report Wizard for RTF reports.

faqs.answer: The price depends on your device integration needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your protocol and device requirements are confirmed.

longForm.heroLead: The Control Pad caps at 30 steps. The PC Software has no cap at all. Every Mya 4 ships with the touch-screen Control Pad, and for most protocols, that's genuinely enough: manual or automated profiles, independent zone control, real-time graphs, all included as standard. But the Control Pad has a real ceiling: 30 steps of up to 16 hours each. If your protocol needs more steps, longer stages, or control over equipment beyond the reaction station itself, the PC Control Software removes that ceiling entirely and adds control of up to 16 third-party devices from one screen. Try it before deciding. Free demo software lets you simulate device control and build schedules without committing to anything.

faqs.question: What vessel sizes are available for the Mya 4?
faqs.answer: Process reaction vessels from 50 to 400 mL, round bottom flasks from 25 to 250 mL, and vials and tubes across seven confirmed diameters.

faqs.question: Why does each vessel size get its own insert?
faqs.answer: Dedicated inserts give genuine heat transfer contact for each vessel size, avoiding the imprecise fit that comes from layering mismatched inserts together.

faqs.question: How do I set up overhead stirring for a very small sample volume?
faqs.answer: Use the Carousel 12 Plus reaction tube, which attaches to the Reflux or Manifold head and enables overhead stirring from as low as 5 mL.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right impeller for a scale-up study?
faqs.answer: Use the Retreat Curve Impeller, purpose-built to mirror the mixing conditions of a large-scale reaction during bench-scale work.

faqs.question: What impeller shapes are available?
faqs.answer: Turbine, anchor, U-shape, centrifugal, and flat, with custom impellers available on request.

faqs.question: Can I integrate a PAT probe with the Mya 4?
faqs.answer: Yes, using the dedicated Blaze Metrics probe lid, a 6-neck glass-filled PTFE lid for the 400 mL process vessel, which also works in standard operation without the probe fitted.

faqs.question: What is the difference between glass and PTFE lids?
faqs.answer: PTFE lids offer improved durability and safety, and are strong enough to support heavier probes and accessories, compared to standard glass lids.

faqs.question: Can I refresh a worn Mya 4 top cover without buying a new unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, the silicone top cover is designed as a low-cost way for existing users to rejuvenate a worn cover.

longForm.heroLead: One insert per vessel size. Never a mismatched stack. Most reaction stations make you improvise: stack a couple of inserts together, hope the fit is close enough. Mya 4's aluminium inserts don't ask you to guess. Every vessel size gets its own dedicated insert, for real heat transfer contact, not an approximation. The same precision runs through the whole accessory range: process vessels shaped to mimic jacketed reactors, flasks and tubes across seven diameters, and a Retreat Curve Impeller built specifically to mirror large-scale mixing conditions at bench scale. PTFE lids, glassware, temperature probes, and even a dedicated lid for the Blaze Metrics probe round out a system built to be configured exactly, not approximately.

sections.title: Mya 4 Vessels and Accessories at a Glance
sections.description: Everything you need to configure Mya 4 precisely: which vessel and insert match your reaction, which stirring and lid options fit, what's available for scale-up and probe integration, and Inkarp installation and service support.
sections.subheading: One insert per vessel size. Never a mismatched stack.
body: Every vessel size gets its own insert, not a generic fit. Anodised aluminium inserts are dedicated per size, explicitly avoiding the need to layer mismatched inserts together.
Process vessels are shaped to behave like real jacketed reactors. Straight sides and a dished base, from 50 to 400 mL, with side arm and baffled options.
Small volumes still get proper overhead stirring. The Carousel 12 Plus reaction tube brings overhead stirring down to as low as 5 mL.
Scale-up gets its own purpose-built impeller. The Retreat Curve Impeller specifically mirrors large-scale mixing conditions during bench-scale work.
PTFE lids trade some material simplicity for real durability. Stronger than glass, built to support heavier probes and accessories.
Third-party probe integration has a dedicated lid. The Blaze Metrics probe fits a specific 6-neck PTFE lid on the 400 mL process vessel, usable in standard operation even without the probe fitted.
Everyday accessories cover the practical side too. Benchtop stands, support rods, a silicone top cover for rejuvenating worn units, and dedicated dosing kits.
Confirmed line: Radleys Mya 4 Vessels and Accessories.
Vessel families: Process Reaction Vessels (50-400 mL), Round Bottom Flasks (25-250 mL), Vials and Tubes.

Dedicated aluminium insert per vessel size; custom inserts available for vials/tubes.

sections.title: Vessel, Insert and Diameter Matching
body: Matching a vessel to its insert, and a tube to its diameter, is what actually determines fit and heat transfer performance, not just capacity.

Process vessels run 50 to 400 mL, shaped with straight sides and a dished base specifically to mimic a jacketed reactor's behavior. Round bottom flasks, drawn from the Carousel 6 Plus range, run 25 to 250 mL in standard or wide-neck versions. Vials and tubes span seven confirmed diameters, and every one of them, along with every vessel size, gets its own dedicated aluminium insert rather than a layered stack.
